R-performance-1 (The export buffers the whole audit log and builds the CSV synchronously on the event loop) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The handler runs `SELECT * FROM audit_events WHERE org_id = $1 ORDER BY
created_at`, loads the rows into an array, builds the whole CSV string with
`rows.map(toCsvLine).join("\n")`, and sends it.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: Cost grows linearly with the organization's history, on a user-facing request: the design's own Context gives about 40 000 events per organization and per month kept seven years, so one export reaches about 3.4 million rows. With `query()` in src/db.ts returning `result.rows` as one array, every row is held in memory, then a second copy as one CSV string, then `map`/`join` run synchronously on the single event loop ("one event loop per instance"), stalling every other request of the instance for the whole build, and a few concurrent exports can exhaust the process memory (a single JS string is also capped near 512 MB). The requirement "every audit event ... oldest first" can be kept while bounding the work: read the rows with a server-side cursor (e.g. `pg-cursor`/`pg-query-stream`, or keyset batches on `(created_at, id)` with a LIMIT), write each batch's CSV lines to the response as a stream honouring backpressure, and select only the exported columns instead of `SELECT *`. Record this choice in the design (replacing "Alternatives considered: none") and add a task that exercises the export on a realistic volume, measuring memory and event-loop delay.
findings.title: The export buffers the whole audit log and builds the CSV synchronously on the event loop

findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: The schema of `audit_events` is not in the repository, so whether an index covers `(org_id, created_at)` could not be checked. Without one, each export scans and sorts a table holding every organization's seven years of events, a cost that grows with the whole table rather than with the organization. Check the existing indexes (and `EXPLAIN` the query); if missing, plan an index on `(org_id, created_at)` — which keyset batching from R-performance-1 also needs — and say so in the design and tasks.
findings.title: No index is planned for the export's filter and sort
